name: sn-add-starting-resource-food
note: Cheat - adds extra food to starting resources.

name: sn-add-starting-resource-gold
note: Cheat - adds extra gold to starting resources.

name: sn-add-starting-resource-stone
note: Cheat - adds extra stone to starting resources.

name: sn-add-starting-resource-wood
note: Cheat - adds extra wood to starting resources.

name: sn-allow-adjacent-dropsites
note: Set to 1 to eliminate the standard requirement for a 1 tile buffer around mills, lumber camps, and mining camps. If set to 0, the 1 tile buffer is enforced as usual.

name: sn-allow-capturing-gaia-units
note: Set > 0 to allow AI player to convert units owned by Gaia.

name: sn-allow-civilian-defense
note: Set to 0 to disable civilian defense, 1 to defend against weak, non-ranged units, 2 for all weak units except warships and units faster than villagers, and 3 for all weak units except warships.

name: sn-allow-civilian-offense
note: Set to 1 to allow villagers to participate as soldiers in town-size attacks. If set to 2, villagers will target enemy villagers and buildings even if defensive military units are available. If set to 0, villagers will only be sent to attack enemy forward towers, without murder holes.

name: sn-allow-gathering-sea-fish-with-villagers
note: Set to 1 to allow villagers to gather deep sea fish in addition to shore fish.

name: sn-allow-serjeant-building
note: Set to 1 to automatically assign Serjeants to a Donjon foundation instead of villagers if available. If there are no available Serjeants a Villager is chosen instead.

name: sn-attack-group-gather-spacing
note: Controls the relative proximity (to the group gather point) that grouped units must be in before the group is considered gathered.

name: sn-attack-group-size-randomness
note: The randomness factor in the attack group size. This sets a cap on the amount of randomness in the minimum attack group size. The randomness factor is set once (when the group is created) and will be between 0 and this number.

name: sn-attack-intelligence
note: Specifies whether the intelligent attack system is used. The intelligent attack system tries to avoid enemy units when attacking and tries to attack from different sides. When used with the sn-attack-coordination set to 2, this can create multifront attacks. Must be 0 (to turn off) and 1 (to turn on).

name: sn-attack-winning-player
note: Controls whether or not the computer player will attack the winning player (if there is more than one to choose from).

name: sn-attack-winning-player-factor
note: The influence the sn-attack-winning-player will have on deciding who to attack if it's set to 1.

name: sn-blot-exploration-map
note: This controls whether or not the computer player re-explores previously explored regions. A value of 1 has the computer player re-explore, a value of 0 does not.

name: sn-blot-size
note: This controls the size of the area that a computer player marks for re-exploration.

name: sn-boar-lure-destination
note: Set to a value from this image to adjust the boar lure destination at the town center. Add 12 to the normal value (0 to 11) to shift the point down to the grid corner. If set to 0, lurers will attempt to reach the center tile of the town center.

name: sn-building-targeting-mode
note: Set to 0 to target all buildings, 1 to ignore walls and gates, or 2 to ignore walls, gates, and dropsites. Please avoid this strategic number, as you may experience targeting failures under certain circumstances.

name: sn-camp-max-distance
note: Sets the maximum distance that lumber camps and mining camps may be placed from a Town Center.

name: sn-cap-civilian-builders
note: Caps the number of builders allocated. Factored in after the percentage is calculated.

name: sn-cap-civilian-explorers
note: Caps the number of civilian explorers allocated. Ignored when set to -1.

name: sn-cap-civilian-gatherers
note: Caps the number of gatherers allocated. Factored in after the percentage is calculated. Ignored when set to -1

name: sn-consecutive-idle-unit-limit
note: Sets the number of consecutive seconds that pass before a group is set to idle if all of its units are idle. This is only used during attack and retreat phases.

name: sn-coop-share-attacking
note: Controls whether allied computer players can attack to defend each other.

name: sn-coop-share-attacking-interval
note: Controls how often this computer player can ask another for help (in seconds).

name: sn-coop-share-information
note: Controls whether or not allied computer players share information about what they uncover (this is not like Cartography; instead, it's analogous to two humans chatting).

name: sn-defer-dropsite-update
note: Set to 1 to defer the dropsite-min-distance update until construction is complete. If set to 0, the dropsite update occurs when the building is placed on the map.

name: sn-disable-attack-groups
note: Set to 1 to disable automatic attack group targeting. Once groups are created, they can be used for defensive attack purposes using TSA. If set to 0, attack groups will perform offensive targeting as usual.

name: sn-disable-builder-assistance
note: Set to 1 to prevent builders from assisting on nearby foundations after their work is complete. If set to 0, they will assist as usual.

name: sn-disable-defend-groups
note: Append flags to disable various defense systems: 1 to disable the defensive (TSA) targeting system, 2 to disable assistance inside sn-safe-town-size, 4 to disable assistance between sn-safe-town-size and sn-maximum-town-size, 8 to disable assistance outside sn-maximum-town-size. When assistance is disabled, please be aware that your units will only respond to attackers within their individual line of sight. If set to 0, units will respond to threats in town as usual.

name: sn-disable-sighted-response-cap
note: Set to 1 to eliminate the cap of 50 on sn-enemy-sighted-response-distance. If set to 0, the cap will remain in effect for changes to sn-enemy-sighted-response-distance.

name: sn-disable-tower-priority
note: Set to 1 to prevent the local targeting system from giving special priority to towers and other fortifications, including town centers and castles. If set to 0, these buildings will receive the usual special priority.

name: sn-disable-trade-evasion
note: Set to 1 to prevent trade carts from abandoning their gold and trade route in order to evade attackers. If set to 0, trade carts will attempt to evade attackers as usual.

name: sn-disable-villager-garrison
note: Set to 3 to prevent villagers from auto-garrisoning for any reason. If set to 2, gaia is ignored and villagers will only garrison for enemy attacks if they can enter a town center. If set to 1, gaia is ignored and villagers will garrison for any enemy attacks. If set to 0, villagers will garrison as usual.

name: sn-do-not-scale-for-difficulty-level
note: Disables the automatic difficulty-scaling.

name: sn-do-not-transport-from-same-zone
note: Set to 1 to influence transport ship behavior.

name: sn-dock-avoidance-factor
note: Set to the avoidance factor for docks in the same zone (body of water). Positive values avoid placement in the same zone, while negative values prefer it.

name: sn-dock-placement-mode
note: Set to 1 to prefer placement toward the front, -1 to prefer placement toward the back, or 0 for standard placement.

name: sn-dock-proximity-factor
note: Set to the proximity factor for docks to be placed relative to one another. Positive values prefer more distance, while negative values prefer less distance.

name: sn-dock-training-filter
note: Set to 1 or 2 to enable the intelligent dock training filter. This will prevent docks from training ships that would likely be useless in their body of water. If set to 1, docks will continue to train in seas that no longer contain recently sighted targets, while 2 will block training. If set to 0, docks will train units without additional consideration.

name: sn-dropsite-separation-distance
note: Set to suggest the minimum distance between dropsites. Higher values can be useful for an escape camp when gatherers are under attack.

name: sn-easier-reaction-percentage
note: Sets the effective reaction percentage (of normal LOS) a computer player unit will use in single-player easier scenario or campaign games.

name: sn-easiest-reaction-percentage
note: Sets the effective reaction percentage (of normal LOS) a computer player unit will use in single-player Easiest level scenario or campaign games.

name: sn-enable-boar-hunting
note: Set to 1 to target deer and boar; if it's set to 2, deer will be ignored.

name: sn-enable-full-vision
note: Unknown. This SN is undocumented.

name: sn-enable-new-building-system
note: Set to 1 only once to request the new building system, featuring simultaneous construction and cancellation control.

name: sn-enable-offensive-priority
note: Set to 1 to enable attack-now and attack groups to target using the priorities set by up-set-offense-priority.

name: sn-enable-patrol-attack
note: Set to 1 to enable the patrol-style local targeting system. When attacking a distant target, this causes units to retarget against nearby sighted units immediately instead of waiting until they are in proximity to the original target.

name: sn-enable-research-queue
note: Controls whether AI players can (or cannot) queue technologies along with units when sn-enable-training-queue is enabled. Set to 1 to enable queued technologies.

name: sn-enable-training-queue
note: Set to values > 0 to allow an additional unit(s) to be queued at each building. If set to 0, buildings will train one unit at a time.

name: sn-enemy-sighted-response-distance
note: Sets the distance inside of which units will be candidates for response to an enemy attack.

name: sn-filter-under-attack
note: Set to 1 or 2 to filter retreat commands to only those units that are under attack. When this is 2, units near threatened units will also be retreated, which may be computationally expensive. If set to 0, the filter is disabled.

name: sn-fishing-boat-whaling-percentage
note: The percentage of fishing ships which will gather from whales.

name: sn-focus-player-number
note: Set to any player number in order to use the "focus-player" identifier in facts and actions.

name: sn-food-dropsite-distance
note: The maximum number of tiles a computer player likes to walk to drop off its food.

name: sn-food-gatherer-percentage
note: Set to configure food gatherers: foodGatherers = ( this + sn-food-modifier-percentage ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-food-modifier-percentage
note: Set to configure food gatherers: foodGatherers = ( sn-food-gatherer-percentage + this ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-free-siege-targeting
note: Add bit flags together to generate a value: 1 = trebuchet; 2 = cannon-galleon. Set a flag for a unit to enable free offensive targeting with attack-now or attack groups. This may result in the targeting of units other than buildings. If set to 0, non-buildings will be ignored unless units must respond due to sn-enemy-sighted-response-distance.

name: sn-garrison-rams
note: Set to 0 to turn off. When on, the CP AI tries (but doesn't always succeed) to put infantry units into rams before the attack group departs.

name: sn-gate-type-for-wall
note: 0 for stone gates, 1 for palisade gates when using the build-gate/can-build-gate command.

name: sn-gather-defense-units
note: Set to 1 to send units to gather untasked defense units more or less around the town center.

name: sn-gather-idle-soldiers-at-center
note: When set to 1, it will "move" the town defense gather point to the "center" (randomized +-6 tiles) of the map. No provision is made if the center is in an unreachable spot. When it's set, all idle and retreating units will try to go to the center. Useful for King of the Hill and similar variants to get the CP to group near the middle.

name: sn-gather-idle-soldiers-at-spawn-point
note: Controls whether idle military units will walk back to the building they were trained out of.

name: sn-gold-dropsite-distance
note: The maximum number of tiles a computer player likes to walk to drop off its gold.

name: sn-gold-gatherer-percentage
note: Set to configure gold gatherers: goldGatherers = ( this + sn-gold-modifier-percentage ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-gold-modifier-percentage
note: Set to configure gold gatherers: goldGatherers = ( sn-gold-gatherer-percentage + this ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-group-commander-selection-method
note: Sets the method by which group commanders are selected. 0 selects the unit with the most hit points. 1 selects the unit with the fewest hit points. 2 selects the unit with the most range. The commander is set once during a group's creation and is only reset when the commander dies.

name: sn-group-form-distance
note: Sets the distance over which attack soldiers will group. Set this value high if buildings that train military units are far apart.

name: sn-group-leader-defense-distance
note: Sets the defense distance for defenders of an important attack group leader.

name: sn-home-exploration-time
note: Set to the maximum amount of time, in seconds, that should be dedicated to exploring the home town center region.

name: sn-ignore-attack-group-under-attack
note: Set to 1 to specify that defensive units should ignore attack-now attack groups under attack.

name: sn-ignore-tower-elevation
note: Set to 1 to ignore elevation when placing towers. If set to 0, the AI will try to seek elevation advantage.

name: sn-initial-attack-delay
note: The forced, initial delay before any computer player attacks (in seconds).

name: sn-initial-attack-delay-type
note: The type of initial attack delay. A value of 1 denotes a delay ended by the build list. A value of 2 uses the sn-initial-attack-delay timeout. A value of 3 allows the computer player to attack after he has been attacked by a non-Gaia player. A value of 0 allows any of the three occurrences to enable attacks.

name: sn-initial-exploration-required
note: The percentage of the map that must be explored by a computer player before any building is allowed.

name: sn-keystates
note: This allows the AI to input ctrl and shift inputs when issuing commands. Setting to 1 corresponds to shift, setting to 2 corresponds to ctrl and setting to 3 corresponds to both.

name: sn-livestock-to-town-center
note: Set to 1 to require livestock, such as sheep, to gather at the town center. If set to 0, they will gather at mills, as well.

name: sn-local-targeting-mode
note: Set to 1 to prioritize attack bonuses and overall damage per hit. If set to 2, units will prioritize targets with high base pierce armor, such as rams; otherwise, they will target as usual. The offensive priority value of a target (-1 to 11) is added to the weight for modes 1 and 2, as well. If set to 0, units will target as usual.

name: sn-lumber-camp-max-distance
note: Sets the maximum-town-size for lumber-camp placement, when non-zero. If set to 0, sn-camp-max-distance will be used instead.

name: sn-max-retask-gather-amount
note: The maximum amount that a gatherer can be told to gather before being allowed to be retasked. Some code may override this.

name: sn-maximum-attack-group-size
note: Sets the maximum size of land-based attack groups.

name: sn-maximum-boat-attack-group-size
note: Sets the maximum size of boat attack groups.

name: sn-maximum-boat-explore-group-size
note: Sets the maximum size of boat exploration groups.

name: sn-maximum-explore-group-size
note: Sets the maximum size of land-based soldier exploration groups.

name: sn-maximum-fish-boat-drop-distance
note: The parameters control how far from a dropsite a given resource type can be before the CP ignores it.

name: sn-maximum-food-drop-distance
note: The parameters control how far from a dropsite a given resource type can be before the CP ignores it.

name: sn-maximum-gaia-attack-response
note: The maximum number of villagers that respond to another civilian getting attacked by a Gaia animal.

name: sn-maximum-garrison-fill
note: Set to the number of units to fill into each garrison target per command. If set to 0, this limit is removed.

name: sn-maximum-gold-drop-distance
note: The parameters control how far from a dropsite a given resource type can be before the CP ignores it.

name: sn-maximum-hunt-drop-distance
note: The parameters control how far from a dropsite a given resource type can be before the CP ignores it.

name: sn-maximum-patrol-distance
note: How far a unit likes to travel from the patrol path, if the unit goes outside this distance on the patrol path, it'll return to patrolling. -1 means no maximum distance.

name: sn-maximum-stone-drop-distance
note: The parameters control how far from a dropsite a given resource type can be before the CP ignores it.

name: sn-maximum-town-size
note: Sets the maximum size of a computer player town.

name: sn-maximum-wood-drop-distance
note: The parameters control how far from a dropsite a given resource type can be before the CP ignores it.

name: sn-mill-max-distance
note: Sets the maximum distance that mills may be placed from a Town Center.

name: sn-minimum-attack-group-size
note: Sets the minimum size of land-based attack groups. A group must meet its minimum size as one of the tasking prerequisites. The game can change this itself during the game.

name: sn-minimum-boar-hunt-group-size
note: The number of villagers a computer player must collect before allowing boars to be hunted for food.

name: sn-minimum-boar-lure-group-size
note: Set to the number of villagers that will be sent in the initial boar luring group.

name: sn-minimum-boat-attack-group-size
note: Sets the minimum size of boat attack groups. A group must meet its minimum size as one of the tasking prerequisites.

name: sn-minimum-boat-explore-group-size
note: Sets the minimum size of boat exploration groups.

name: sn-minimum-civilian-explorers
note: Sets a minimum number of civilian explorers.

name: sn-minimum-explore-group-size
note: Sets the minimum size of land-based soldier exploration groups. A group must meet its minimum size as one of the tasking prerequisites.

name: sn-minimum-number-hunters
note: Set to force hunting. For best results when hunting boar, set this in conjunction with sn-minimum-boar-hunt-group-size.

name: sn-minimum-town-size
note: Sets the minimum size of a computer player town.

name: sn-minimum-water-body-size-for-dock
note: The minimum number of tiles (in surface area) that a body of water must be for a Dock to be placed on it.

name: sn-mining-camp-max-distance
note: Sets the maximum-town-size for mining-camp placement, when non-zero. If set to 0, sn-camp-max-distance will be used instead.

name: sn-mule-cart-dropsite-placement
note: Controls the placement of newly constructed mule carts.

name: sn-number-attack-groups
note: Sets the desired number of land-based attack groups. Sn-percent-attack-soldiers generally works better.

name: sn-number-boat-attack-groups
note: Sets the desired number of boat attack groups. Setting sn-percent-attack-boat usually works better.

name: sn-number-boat-explore-groups
note: Sets the desired number of military boat exploration groups. This is not affected by sn-total-number-explorers.

name: sn-number-civilian-militia
note: Set to the maximum number of villagers who may be used to attack the enemy.

name: sn-number-explore-groups
note: Sets the desired number of land-based soldier exploration groups.

name: sn-number-forward-builders
note: The number of villagers a computer player uses to build outside of an enemy town. Forward builders refer specifically to those villagers that must board a Transport to cross over water that cannot otherwise be pathed, either because players are on islands, or because other forms of access have been walled-off. It is not necessary to specify forward builders, unless the villagers need to board a Transport.

name: sn-number-garrison-units
note: Set to the number of units that will garrison per command. If set to 0, it will default to the maximum of 40.

name: sn-number-tasked-units
note: Set to the number of units to require per group tasked by up-target-objects or up-target-point. The last group sent by a command may not reach the minimum required number. It's possible that no units will be sent to some of the last remote targets. If set to 0, units will be spread in order to ensure balanced group sizes to all remote targets.

name: sn-object-repair-level
note: Add bit flags together to generate a value: 0 = wonder; 1 = castle, monastery; 2 = town-center; 4 = barracks; 8 = archery-range; 16 = stable; 32 = siege-workshop; 64 = dock; 128 = market; 256 = university; 512 = blacksmith; 1024 = lumber-camp, mining-camp, mill; 2048 = house; 4096 = towers; 8192 = walls and gates; 16384 = siege weapons. For scenarios and campaigns, the default is 1 for compatibility.

name: sn-percent-attack-boats
note: Sets the percentage of defense boats that will be sent into battle (modified for difficulty level) the next time attack-now is issued. All newly created boats are defense boats by default, and will remain defense boats until attack-now is issued. Both attack soldiers and attack boats will attack when attack-now is issued. This SN only needs to be set once, but it can be changed as needed.

name: sn-percent-attack-soldiers
note: Sets the percentage of defense soldiers that will be sent into battle (modified for difficulty level) the next time attack-now is issued. All newly created soldiers are defense soldiers by default, and will remain defense soldiers until attack-now is issued. For example, if 10 soldiers were defending a town, and sn-percent-attack-soldiers was set to 50, then 5 soldiers will form an attack group and attack. This SN only needs to be set once, but it can be changed as needed. sn-percent-attack-soldiers works best when not using sn-number-defend-groups.

name: sn-percent-building-cancellation
note: Set to the maximum allowable completion percentage for building cancellation.

name: sn-percent-civilian-builders
note: AoE1 only. Controls the normal, formula-based percentage of builders allocated.

name: sn-percent-civilian-explorers
note: Caps the number of villagers assigned to explore to the given percentage.

name: sn-percent-civilian-gatherers
note: AoE1 only. Controls the normal, formula-based percentage of gatherers allocated.

name: sn-percent-enemy-sighted-response
note: Sets the percentage of idle troops that will respond to another unit being attacked.

name: sn-percent-exploration-required
note: Sets the minimum amount of exploration that a computer player must have accomplished before being allowed to retask civilian explorers.

name: sn-percent-half-exploration
note: The percentage of map exploration that allows the computer player to task down to half the number of explorers.

name: sn-placement-fail-delta
note: Set to the value that will be added to the placement distance set by up-set-placement-data for every pass that a building cannot be placed.

name: sn-placement-to-center
note: Set to 1 to force place-control to use the map center as the second point of reference for placement. The first point of reference is set with up-set-placement-data. If set to 0, the active target player's nearest building will become the second point of reference instead, once discovered. If sn-target-player-number is 0, the target enemy will be determined by sn-attack-winning-player.

name: sn-placement-zone-size
note: Set to the size of the tile zone used for forward and controlled building placement. All build commands store this value and the up-set-placement-data information with each successful call. For every pass that a building cannot be placed, its zone size will be increased from this starting point.

name: sn-preferred-mill-placement
note: Set to 0 for forage, 1 for deer, or 2 for shore fish.

name: sn-preferred-settlement-placement
note: Controls the resource that settlements are placed nearby.

name: sn-preferred-storage-pit-placement
note: Controls the preferred resource the AI will place its storage pits nearby. Return of Rome DLC only.

name: sn-preferred-trade-distance
note: Set to the preferred distance between local and remote trade buildings.

name: sn-profiling-threshold
note:
Sets a performance threshold that if exceeded will cause the game will be stopped and the debug screen will appear. Ignored if set to -1 (the default). It's unknown which performance metric this SN is using.

For this SN to work, you must also add the Steam launch parameters AIDEBUGGING and AISCRIPTPROFILING. To set launch parameters, open Steam => Right click the game in the Library view => click Properties => and type the launch parameters, separated by spaces (not commas).

According to offwo, the DE devs give a rough guideline that this shouldn't trigger at 1000 and under 600 was ideal, but offwo suggests that setting this SN to 1500-2000 is fine for a custom AI. Setting this SN to a higher value like 10000 can help find jump freezes too without having to wait a long time.

Further guidance from Aleph: One benefit is that the AISCRIPTPROFILING debug screen in conjunction with saving the player number in a goal makes it very easy to identify the offending player in the case of a freeze. This is a great improvement over the old AoC tournaments. In contrast, unlike freezes, identifying the cause of a crash is still virtually impossible except by the devs.

The downside to sn-profiling-threshold is that we're not clear on how the engine determines when the threshold is met, or what exactly the number is supposed to represent.

As far as I can tell, it is decided within the script pass itself and triggers on a specific rule (which is displayed), but beyond that I have no idea. According to a guideline given by the devs, the AI should never trigger the profiling threshold on a setting of 1000. However, I've sometimes seen it trigger on settings as high as 3000 without the AI exceeding optimal performance (333ms between ticks), including a case of DEfault repeatedly triggering it in dark age, and Illuminati triggering it just by sending 12 debug chat messages. It is possible that the system is simply flawed, and runs a risk of intering with the smooth running of tournament games if left enabled.

name: sn-random-placement-factor
note: A number that gets added into the placement of the computer player to randomize building placement (off of the calculated ideal).

name: sn-remove-units-from-control-groups
note: Unknown. This SN is undocumented.

name: sn-retask-gather-amount
note: The minimum amount that a gatherer must gather before the computer player allows him to be retasked to another resource type. Some code may override this.

name: sn-safe-town-size
note: If an enemy building is inside both sn-maximum-town-size and the region specified by this sn, it will be targeted by defensive units. If the building is inside sn-maximum-town-size, but outside this region, it will be targeted only if it belongs to the player specified by sn-target-player-number.

name: sn-scale-maximum-attack-group-size
note: The scaling factor for the maximum attack group size. Added to sn-minimum-attack-group-size when the tactical AI does its scaling.

name: sn-scale-minimum-attack-group-size
note: The scaling factor for the minimum attack group size. Added to sn-minimum-attack-group-size when the tactical AI does its scaling.

name: sn-scaling-frequency
note: Sets the number of minutes that pass between each scaling inside the tactical AI.

name: sn-sentry-distance
note: Sets the distance at which the town is defended.

name: sn-sentry-distance-variation
note: Sets the amount of allowable variation in the defense distances.

name: sn-special-attack-influence1
note: Sets the multiplier used for the special attack type 1 rating in computer player target evaluation. Must be > 0 to influence the computer player toward attacking the special type 1, < 0 to influence the computer player away from attacking the special type 1.

name: sn-special-attack-influence2
note: Sets the multiplier used for the special attack type 2 rating in computer player target evaluation. Must be > 0 to influence the computer player toward attacking the special type 2, < 0 to influence the computer player away from attacking the special type 2.

name: sn-special-attack-influence3
note: Sets the multiplier used for the special attack type 3 rating in computer player target evaluation. Must be > 0 to influence the computer player toward attacking the special type 3, < 0 to influence the computer player away from attacking the special type 3.

name: sn-special-attack-type1
note: Set to 1 to target monasteries and monks carrying relics.

name: sn-special-attack-type2
note: Set to any unit, building, or group id to direct attacks.

name: sn-special-attack-type3
note: Set to 1 to target wonders.

name: sn-stone-dropsite-distance
note: The maximum number of tiles a computer player likes to walk to drop off its stone.

name: sn-stone-gatherer-percentage
note: Set to configure stone gatherers: stoneGatherers = ( this + sn-stone-modifier-percentage ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-stone-modifier-percentage
note: Set to configure stone gatherers: stoneGatherers = ( sn-stone-gatherer-percentage + this ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-target-player-number
note: Set to the number of the player that should be targeted for attack. If this sn is set to -1, initiating an attack will instead provide assistance to allies. When set to 0, sn-attack-winning-player will determine the target. Setting this to a player that cannot be attacked (an ally or the AI itself) will result in undefined behavior. You can also use this value with the "target-player" identifier in facts and actions.

name: sn-target-point-adjustment
note: Set to adjust the tile positioning of up-target-point toward 1:left, 2:top, 3:right, 4:bottom, 5:middle, 6:precise. If set to 0, actions will be directed to the absolute left-most point of a tile. If set to precise, you must directly pass a valid precise point goal pair (point x100 for precision) to up-target-point.

name: sn-task-ungrouped-soldiers
note: Controls whether or not ungrouped computer player soldiers get tasked to spread out and guard the computer player's general town area.

name: sn-total-number-explorers
note: Caps the total number of land explorers allocated.

name: sn-town-center-placement
note: Set to the building type to emulate for town center placement. If set to 0, the town center will be placed as usual.

name: sn-ttkfactor-scalar
note: Time to kill an object scalar (in seconds). The scalar is a percentage. Likely affects retargeting against nearby units.

name: sn-unexplored-construction
note: Set to 1 to allow the AI to construct buildings on unexplored tiles. If set to 0, the AI will have to directly explore tiles in order to build there as usual. Please do not enable this without #load-if-not-defined REVEAL-NORMAL.

name: sn-use-by-type-max-gathering
note: Controls whether or not logical, type-specific gatherer requirements are placed on the quantity of resources gatherers must collect before being allowed to be retasked.

name: sn-villager-attack-reset
note: If set to 0, disables the auto-villager attack reset so you can attack distant units/targets with villagers.

name: sn-wall-targeting-mode
note: Set to 1 to allow military units to automatically target nearby walls and gates. If set to 0, they will likely be ignored.

name: sn-warship-targeting-mode
note: Set to 1 to cause warships to target based on the unit with the shortest range in the group against fortifications. Set to 2 to eliminate the range check. If set to 0, warship groups will target based on the unit with the longest range.

name: sn-whaling-max-distance
note: Controls how far from a dropsite a whale can be before the CP ignores it.

name: sn-wild-animal-exploration
note: Allows wild horses, wild camel and bactrian camels to explore.

name: sn-wood-dropsite-distance
note: The maximum number of tiles a computer player likes to walk to drop off its wood.

name: sn-wood-gatherer-percentage
note: Set to configure wood gatherers: woodGatherers = ( this + sn-wood-modifier-percentage ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-wood-modifier-percentage
note: Set to configure wood gatherers: woodGatherers = ( sn-wood-gatherer-percentage + this ) * gathererTotal * 0.01 + 0.5.

name: sn-zero-priority-distance
note: Sets the distance at which a computer player's order for a unit is set to a priority of 0.
